section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Bernoulli Trials
section_1.content: Define the building block: a Bernoulli trial. It is a random experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (S) or Failure (F), with probabilities p and (1-p) respectively.
section_1.example: Visualizing a coin flip: Heads (p=0.5) vs. Tails (1-p=0.5). Imagine a light switch flipping between ON and OFF.

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
section_2.content: Introduce the four criteria (BINS): Binary outcomes, Independent trials, Number of trials is fixed, and Probability is constant. Visualize a 'tree diagram' expanding as trials increase.
section_2.example: A basketball player shooting 5 free throws. Each shot is a trial; successes are 'baskets' and failures are 'misses', with a fixed 70% accuracy.

section_3.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
section_3.content: Explain the formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Break it into components: C(n,k) for combinations (order doesn't matter), p^k for success, and q^(n-k) for failures.
section_3.example: Animation showing the paths to achieve exactly 2 baskets in 3 shots: (S,S,F), (S,F,S), (F,S,S). The formula calculates these distinct paths automatically.

section_4.title: Visualizing Probability Distributions
section_4.content: Use a histogram to show how changing 'p' and 'n' shifts the distribution's shape. Mention Mean (np) and Variance (npq) as the 'center' and 'spread' of the graph.
section_4.example: A bar chart showing 10 coin flips. As we increase trials, the histogram begins to resemble a Bell Curve (Normal distribution approximation).

section_5.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
section_5.content: Summary of when to use the binomial distribution in industry or research. Emphasize checking for 'Independence' as the most common pitfall.
section_5.example: A robotic arm on an assembly line: Calculating the probability that exactly 3 out of 10 microchips are defective, given a known defect rate of 2%.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
